validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: I re-derived the proposal's load-bearing claims from the code myself rather than accepting them, and every one held: the four skip-eligibility call sites and the three inverted readers of scheduleIsRecurring are exactly as enumerated, getNextDateAfter's null-past-the-end behaviour is already asserted by an existing passing test, setNextDate's guard is the drop point, the two AQL envelopes are byte-for-byte identical, the page model does return a lazy Locator read by non-retrying calls, and ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134 is the only unguarded pass-through in its file. The two behavioural fixes have exactly identified root causes. The e2e work is mechanical and its one real trap — that page.evaluate cannot close over a Node binding — is understood and designed around. The confidence is not higher for two reasons: nothing was executed (node_modules is absent, so reproduced is false and the new unit tests are written but unrun), and QA 2 is dropped on a reasoning argument about serialisation I verified by reading but did not demonstrate by firing two concurrent skips. Both are resolvable by the first person to run the tests.
validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #61 bundles eight follow-ups from PR #59 (merged 2026-10-04). Six are e2e-test hygiene; two are real defects in shipped code. Re-verified every claim against the code.

Review 1 (menu introspection does not auto-wait) is real: _openNthScheduleMenu returns a lazy Locator that consumers read with count()/allTextContents(), neither of which retries. Review 2 (index-vs-payee incoherence) is real as written — payee locators are built and asserted toHaveCount(1), then two assertions use raw indices. Review 3 ([AI] title) is not a change to this repository; PR #59 is merged and history already carries [AI]. Review 4 (duplicated $send('query',...) envelope) is real — two byte-for-byte identical 12-key objects, and page.evaluate cannot close over a Node binding so the fix must be a Node-side helper. Review 5 (redundant open/dismiss/re-open) is real.

QA 1 (exhausted recurrence still offers Skip; silent no-op) is real and its root cause is confirmed: scheduleIsRecurring only tests value.type === 'recur', while setNextDate guards on getNextDateAfter returning non-null. An existing passing test already asserts getNextDateAfter returns null for exactly the exhausted fixture QA describes. The primitive exists and is tested; the UI asks a weaker question than the write does.

QA 2 (two concurrent skips advance next_date twice) does not hold as diagnosed and is dropped. runMutator is sequential(_runMutator) over one module-level queue, skip-next-date is registered mutator(undoable(...)), and runHandler routes every mutating handler through that queue — on the API path too. What QA observed is precisely what serialised execution produces.

QA 3 (React controlled/uncontrolled warnings) is real with a single-line cause: useScheduleEdit's nullable name reaches Input unguarded, while two sibling inputs in the same file already carry the || '' guard.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Three distinct causes. (1) The UI and the write ask different questions: four skip-eligibility sites call scheduleIsRecurring ('is this a recurrence at all?') while setNextDate asks the strictly stronger 'does getNextDateAfter return a date?', which is false once the recurrence is exhausted. PR #59 introduced the weaker predicate, so the UI now offers an action the server drops. (2) useScheduleEdit's field state is nullable by type and ScheduleEditForm renders fields.name into a controlled Input without the || '' guard its payee and account siblings already have — the only unguarded pass-through in the file. (3) The e2e page model returns a lazy Locator to callers reading it with non-retrying Playwright calls, while the test grew a second index-based path alongside the payee-based one, plus a duplicated AQL envelope and a redundant open/dismiss cycle.
validated_work_order.approach: Three changes in dependency order. (A) Add scheduleIsSkippable(dateCond, nextDate) to loot-core shared/schedules.ts: scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond) && getNextDateAfter(dateCond, nextDate) != null, short-circuiting false on a null/undefined nextDate. It reuses getNextDateAfter rather than reimplementing occurrence logic, so the UI predicate and the setNextDate write are driven by the same function and cannot drift. This is a new function rather than a widened scheduleIsRecurring because three callers read that predicate inverted to decide whether Complete is offered, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion — one predicate cannot serve both questions. Then swap the four skip-eligibility call sites, passing the row's next_date; all four already select '*' so next_date is in hand. (B) value={fields.name} becomes value={fields.name || ''} at ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134, matching lines 159 and 175. The reducer's initial null is left alone: it is read for truthiness in the duplicate-name check and save path, where null and '' are equally falsy. Both warnings come from that one prop. (C) e2e hygiene: await expect(menu).toBeVisible() once inside _openNthScheduleMenu so all three consumers inherit the wait; widen the row parameter of three helpers to number | Locator so the test's existing payee locators replace raw indices without disturbing the four index callers; hoist a module-level Node-side aqlQuery<T> owning the duplicated $send('query') envelope, with the split-transfer test's three browser-side queries moving out through it (a page.evaluate callback is serialised and cannot close over a Node binding); delete the redundant open/count-0/Escape block so one exact-list assertion carries the absence of Skip; add a console assertion modelled on command-bar.test.ts, filtered by regex to the two React warning texts rather than by console type.

risks: scheduleIsSkippable calls getNextDateAfter on every render of every schedule row. getNextDateAfter loops up to MAX_ADVANCE_ATTEMPTS (7) times, each iteration constructing a Condition and calling rschedule's occurrences(), so this is materially more work than the single getValue() scheduleIsRecurring does. In the common case it returns on the first iteration. The three useMemo sites are unaffected; SchedulesTable's row computes canSkip per row per render and is not memoised. If a large schedule list shows a measurable regression, memoising per schedule id is the follow-up — not added here, because there is no evidence of a problem yet.

ScheduleEditForm.tsx, useScheduleEdit.ts and SchedulesTable.tsx all carry // @ts-strict-ignore, so the ScheduleEditForm change is unchecked by the strict plugin. The loot-core predicate is in a grandfathered file too, but its new signature is explicitly typed and the call sites are in files that are checked.

The three canBeCompleted sites keep reading scheduleIsRecurring inverted, leaving two closely-named predicates in the codebase, one of which is correct for skipping and one of which is not. A future reader could reasonably collapse them and reintroduce this bug. Worth a comment on scheduleIsRecurring saying it answers a different question; the new function's doc comment carries it, but scheduleIsRecurring's own doc was left alone to keep the diff to one new function.

AC-1's fixture cannot be built through the UI at all, because ScheduleEditModal builds its initial schedule without an endMode and recurConfigToRSchedule defaults to 'never'. QA must construct it through the API or a synced budget to reproduce the original finding at all. This makes AC-1 the hardest criterion to verify and the easiest to wave through — hold QA to it specifically.

The e2e work is unverifiable in CI. .sdlc/config.yml sets verify.e2e to the empty string (line 172) and the CI workflow exits 0 when it is empty, so no Playwright assertion in this plan gates anything. AC-3 is the only criterion that does. The four review findings are real cleanups but will not be caught if they regress.
out_of_scope: Review 3 — retitling PR #59 with the [AI] prefix. Not a change to this repository: the fix is `gh pr edit`, and .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md is on the forbidden-paths list, so no file here can express it. The finding's premise has also expired — PR #59 is merged (2026-10-04), not open — and the merge commit 0fb77b4 does carry [AI], so history is compliant.

QA 2 — two concurrent skips advancing next_date twice. Dropped because the stated cause does not exist and the stated fix would be wrong. runMutator is sequential(_runMutator) over one module-level queue, skip-next-date is registered mutator(undoable(skipNextDate)), and runHandler routes every mutating handler through that queue; the API path reaches the same runHandler. What QA observed is what serialised execution produces, and a compare-and-swap would turn two legitimate sequential skips into one, turning a cosmetic double-advance into a real lost action.

The reframed residual from QA 2: a retry of schedule/skip-next-date after a timeout — network retry, sync re-delivery, a client firing twice — advances next_date twice, because the queue makes it a fresh sequential skip rather than a duplicate to ignore. Closing that needs a caller-supplied idempotency key or a server-side dedupe token: a new handler argument, a decision about sync replay, and a change to the undo boundary. A feature, not a small fix; belongs in its own issue. The UI cannot trigger it — the menu closes on click — which is why severity is minor.

Widening scheduleIsRecurring in place instead of adding scheduleIsSkippable. Three call sites read it inverted for canBeCompleted and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion; changing its meaning would silently change Complete's visibility and the preview list for exhausted recurrences, neither of which any finding asks for. Covered by AC-2 as an explicit guard.

Making setNextDate report the no-op instead of dropping it — QA's own suggested alternative for QA 1. Rejected: it changes a handler's return contract and the API surface to fix a menu-visibility question better answered where the question is asked. The UI needs eligibility up front regardless, since a client cannot learn from an absent error that an action would have been dropped.

Adding a component test for the ScheduleEditForm null guard. Rejected on cost: ScheduleEditForm pulls in useScheduleEdit, which needs live queries, redux and modals, and no existing desktop-client component test mounts anything that heavy. The console assertion plus AC-4 cover it at a fraction of the setup.
Enabling Playwright in CI so AC-5 through AC-7 gate something. That is a change to .sdlc/config.yml and .github/workflows, both on the forbidden-paths list.

alternatives_considered.approach: Follow QA 1's stated remedy: drop setNextDate's `newNextDate != null` guard and surface the no-op to the caller instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the wrong layer. The symptom is a menu item that does nothing when clicked, decided in the UI four files away. The null guard is load-bearing — getNextDateAfter legitimately returns null for an exhausted recurrence, and shared/schedules.test.ts:1042-1050 asserts it. Removing it would turn a correct no-op into a write of null into schedules_next_date. The UI needs eligibility up front regardless, since a client cannot learn from an absent error that an action would have been dropped.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 1 by teaching scheduleIsRecurring itself to check for a remaining occurrence, leaving the four call sites untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is the smaller diff and it is wrong. Three sites call the predicate inverted to decide whether Complete is offered, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it to decide whether to expand preview dates — for which 'is this recurring?' is the right question and 'is this skippable?' is not. One predicate cannot serve both. The new function costs four one-line call-site edits and leaves every other meaning intact.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 2 as reported, with a compare-and-swap on schedules_next_date keyed on the next_date that was read.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no race for it to close. runMutator is a single serialised queue, so two skips already run one after the other and the second legitimately reads the first's committed write. A CAS would make the second skip fail — a user pressing Skip twice would see the second press do nothing, and a client retrying after a timeout would silently lose the retry. It trades a cosmetic double-advance for a real lost action.

alternatives_considered.approach: For review 2 and 5, delete the payee locators and the index-independence comment and keep the raw indices, on the grounds that they are correct today and fail loudly on drift.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer already granted the indices are correct; the objection is that the comment claims a guarantee the test does not keep. Deleting the locators removes the better mechanism to satisfy the weaker one. The chosen fix uses the locators the test already built and asserted toHaveCount(1) on, so the comment becomes true instead of being deleted.

alternatives_considered.approach: For review 4, hoist only the 12-key envelope object to module scope and spread it into both page.evaluate callbacks.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not work. A page.evaluate callback is serialised and evaluated in the browser; it cannot reference a Node-scope binding, so the spread would throw a ReferenceError. Deduplicating the envelope requires hoisting a Node-side function that owns its own evaluate — which is why the split-transfer test's three queries move out of the browser rather than the envelope merely moving up a scope.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 3 in useScheduleEdit by seeding the reducer's initial state with name: '' instead of null.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A wider edit with no gain over the one the file already calls for. state.fields.name is read for truthiness in the duplicate-name check and the save path, where '' and null are both falsy, so the behaviour is identical — but it touches the state contract rather than the render site, and lines 159 and 175 already establish the render-site convention this codebase follows.

assumptions: verify.e2e is the empty string at .sdlc/config.yml:172, so no Playwright assertion in this plan gates CI. I read the config; I did not run the workflow.
scheduleIsRecurring has exactly the call sites grep found. I did not add a new one; I am adding scheduleIsSkippable alongside it.

All four skip-eligibility sites hold the full schedule entity from a q('schedules')…select('*') query and so have next_date available. ScheduleEntity.next_date is non-optional. I did not verify at runtime that a row's next_date is never null in practice; the predicate short-circuits on null regardless.

The @actual-app/api send path reaches the same runHandler the desktop client does, via platform/server/connection. This is what makes QA 2's diagnosis wrong; I traced the import in packages/api/methods.ts and the server receiver, but did not execute an API call to observe the serialisation.

A React controlled input given value={null} produces both recorded warnings — the null rejection and then the uncontrolled-to-controlled transition on first keystroke. Standard React behaviour, corroborated by the file's sibling guards, but I could not run the dev server here: node_modules is absent.
ScheduleEditModal builds a new schedule without an endMode, so the exhausted-recurrence fixture cannot be produced through the UI and QA must build it through the API or a synced budget.
unknowns: Whether the Schedules table has a schedule count large enough for the extra getNextDateAfter call per row to matter. No budget-size data and no profiling; the risk is stated but unmeasured.

Whether some other caller — a plugin, a script, an importer — constructs a schedule whose date condition is a recur with an exhausted end and depends on Skip being offered. Grep found only the four UI sites and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, but plugins live outside this repository.
Whether the reviewer would accept the console-assertion addition to the e2e test as belonging in this ticket, or as scope creep on a file that already carries four changes.

What the correct behaviour is for Complete on an exhausted recurrence — whether it too is a silent no-op elsewhere. This plan leaves it alone because no finding raises it, but AC-2 records the current behaviour as the thing to preserve rather than as correct.
residual_risks: Duplicate delivery of schedule/skip-next-date — a network retry, a sync re-delivery, a client firing twice — advances next_date twice. The mutator queue guarantees the two calls are serialised, not that they are the same request. Closing this needs an idempotency key, a feature with its own design questions about sync replay and the undo boundary.

Nothing in CI runs Playwright, so AC-5, AC-6 and AC-7 — three of the five review findings — can regress silently. Only AC-3 gates. Gating them would mean changing .sdlc/config.yml and .github/workflows, both on the forbidden-paths list.

The QA 1 fix hides the menu item rather than surfacing why. A user with an exhausted recurrence who remembers the item being there gets no explanation. The alternative was rejected above; this is the accepted cost.

QA goes here first: AC-1 is the one criterion that cannot be checked by exercising the UI, because ScheduleEditModal cannot build an exhausted recurrence. If AC-1 is waved through without the API/sync fixture, the ticket's one behavioural fix is unverified.
validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate. plan/critique.json is an empty object — the critic wrote nothing, so there is no critique to accept or dismiss, and the council's third round is effectively a single-planner plan that I audited rather than arbitrated between. I am recording that plainly rather than manufacturing agreement; where the proposal and I differ, it is my edit, not the critic's.

The proposal is sound and I kept its shape. Its root causes are correct, its four call-site edits are the right ones, and its decision to add scheduleIsSkippable rather than widen scheduleIsRecurring is right for a reason I confirmed: three sites read that predicate inverted for Complete and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions reads it for preview expansion, so one predicate genuinely cannot serve both questions.

Two things I checked hardest, because that is where this plan could be wrong. QA 2: I did not take the drop on faith. The report says setNextDate has no compare-and-swap and implies two calls interleave. I read runMutator (mutators.ts:97), the sequenceState closure (shared/async.ts:22-28), the handler registration (app.ts:847) and runHandler's routing (mutators.ts:52-56), then traced the API path from packages/api/methods.ts through the server receiver at platform/server/connection/index.ts:56. All of it confirms one serialised queue every mutator shares, on the API path too. The drop is correct, and a CAS would be actively wrong — it would turn a user's second deliberate skip into a lost action. I kept the reframing as a residual: the real gap is idempotency under retry, which is a feature with its own design questions and belongs in its own issue.

QA 1: confirmed rather than doubted, because the existing test at shared/schedules.test.ts:1042-1050 already asserts getNextDateAfter returns null for exactly the exhausted fixture QA describes. The write really is dropped; the UI really is asking a weaker question. The fix reuses that function rather than reimplementing occurrence logic, so predicate and write cannot drift.

My one substantive edit, and the reason I am not simply adopting: the proposal asks for a console assertion filtered to 'error or warning'. command-bar.test.ts:64-95, the pattern it cites, filters with a regex over the warning text precisely because a bare type filter catches unrelated dev-mode noise. Against the demo fixture that would make the new guard flaky, and a flaky guard is worse than none because it trains people to re-run. I narrowed the filter to the two React controlled/uncontrolled warning texts. That is my correction, not the critic's.

Nothing the proposal dropped contradicted a decision in plan/brief.md — the brief records nothing decided and no prior plan rejection, so the issue body was the whole input and there was no person-settled judgement for a finding to run into. Nothing in the file list touches .sdlc/memory/**, docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md, docs/ui.md or .github/**; review 3 is deferred precisely because the only way to satisfy it is a gh pr edit and its premise has expired now that PR #59 is merged.

Residual disagreement I did not resolve: I share the proposal's concern that adding scheduleIsSkippable beside scheduleIsRecurring leaves two closely-named predicates with different meanings and no comment on the older one to say so. I kept its decision not to edit scheduleIsRecurring's doc comment, on diff-size grounds, but I am recording it as a live hazard rather than agreeing it is tidied away.
